clue.text: Certify switch varying direct and alternating current

indicators.note: something varying changes its form, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged
to switch two things is to swap their places, so the two parts are joined in the opposite order to the clue

blocks.note: AC is the standard abbreviation for alternating current
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An electrician certifies a switch that can handle both direct and alternating current.
explanation.walkthrough: The electrical surface hides that 'direct' is just fodder; after the swap the alternating current comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit someone is to give official approval of their competence, which is what certifying means.

clue.text: College formerly imbued with this place's sense of unity

indicators.note: something imbued with a quality has it soaked into it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for college
once means formerly
here is this place

explanation.surface: A college used to be full of a team spirit belonging to this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Coherence is the quality of forming a unified, consistent whole, so a sense of unity.

clue.text: See doctor about a large volume of saline solution

indicators.note: about suggests turning things round, so the letters are shuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient is told to see a doctor about receiving a large saline drip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the anagram signal but is the abbreviation; the medical saline solution is really salty water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Sea is an arm of the Indian Ocean, a vast body of salt water.

clue.text: What may be seen as close to prison?

definitions.text: What may be seen as close to prison?

blocks.clueFragment: What may be seen as close to prison?
blocks.note: surface reading: an institution that is almost a jail
setter's reading: the close of the word prison is its final letter, and that same letter sits at the exact middle of the first word of the answer

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what institution is nearly a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Close as 'near' hides close as 'end': the last letter of prison is N, which is the centre letter of DETENTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A detention centre is a place where people are held in custody, an institution very like a jail.

clue.text: Byzantine patterns in part of church

indicators.note: Byzantine means intricate and convoluted, so the letters are tangled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Byzantine mosaics decorate part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm crossing the nave of a cross-shaped church building.

clue.text: Screen opening of movie on demand

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only the start of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of movie
to ask for something is to demand it

explanation.surface: A cinema screens the opening of a film whenever a viewer requests it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places one part before the other in this down-reading sense of joining; 'Screen' looks like a cinema noun but is a verb meaning to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: To mask something is to conceal or shield it from view, the hiding sense of screen.

clue.text: Taking care of funny doctor

indicators.note: taking means removing, so the abbreviation is subtracted from the word

blocks.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
comedic means funny

explanation.surface: Someone looks after an amusing doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking care of' reads as one phrase meaning looking after; it splits into 'Taking' (remove) and 'care of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A medic is an informal word for a physician or medical worker.

clue.text: I'm surprised date might suggest this before eating

definitions.text: date might suggest this before eating

blocks.note: first meaning: a British exclamation of astonishment

blocks.clueFragment: date might suggest this before eating
blocks.note: second meaning: the fruit asking to have its pit removed before being eaten

explanation.walkthrough: 'Date' is the fruit, not a romantic outing; it has a hard pit that is removed before eating. The exclamation is old-fashioned British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild exclamation of astonishment and also a literal request to have one's pit taken out.

clue.text: Surge of rising river when escaping its banks

indicators.note: in a down entry rising reads from bottom to top, so the river runs backwards
the banks are the outer edges, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A river rises and floods over its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: The flood picture makes 'escaping its banks' look like the definition, but it trims the small word.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to churn and foam, as surging water does; both describe violent heaving movement.

clue.text: System satisfied Head of Department at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the following three words

blocks.note: a need that is satisfied has been met
the initial letters of these three words

explanation.surface: An organisational system pleased the head of department when it was first introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: HOD is also the usual abbreviation for Head of Department, so the initials double as a familiar label.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is an orderly procedure or way of doing things, a common synonym for system.

clue.text: Entrance having rounded cross-section

indicators.note: to round on something is to turn back on it, so the combined pieces are read from end to start

blocks.note: a rood is a crucifix, the cross in a church
a section is a part

explanation.surface: A doorway is described as having a curved profile when cut through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross-section' reads as one technical term but splits into two pieces, the church cross and a section.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapdoor is a hinged door in a floor or ceiling, a way in, so an entrance.

clue.text: Way to encourage swimmer

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: Someone describes the best way to cheer on a swimmer in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Swimmer is the playful definition: a fish is a swimmer, and this one gives caviar.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish, a creature that swims, so a swimmer by crossword whimsy.

clue.text: Unknown Southern Greek island's last to come to the fore

Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: An obscure Greek island in the south finally gains prominence.
explanation.walkthrough: The island's final E moves to its front before the southern S is added.

clue.text: Pigment Cezanne habitually makes use of in a revolutionary way

indicators.note: the answer uses letters already sitting inside the neighbouring words
revolving turns things round, so the concealed letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the painter's name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: The painter Cézanne regularly used a certain pigment in a radical way.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading backwards from the H of habitually through the end of Cezanne gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish dye from a shrub, used to colour hair and skin, so a pigment.

clue.text: 12 like any nina (and this one especially)

definitions.text: 12 like any nina (and this one especially)

blocks.note: surface reading: secret, as a message concealed in a crossword grid always is
setter's reading: this answer is itself split across two separated lights, so it is concealed in the grid more than most

explanation.walkthrough: 12 points to the answer at 12 across, SECRET. A nina is a message concealed in a crossword grid; this answer is split into HID and DEN on two distant lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Something secret is concealed from view, and a nina is by nature a concealed message in the grid.

clue.text: Quibbled with Chosen One lacking sense earlier

indicators.note: earlier means the second item described comes before the first

blocks.note: a nit is a fool, someone lacking sense
picked means chosen

explanation.surface: Someone argued pettily with the Chosen One, who had shown poor judgement before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chosen One' reads as a single messianic title but splits; 'One lacking sense' is the fool. A nit is British slang for a foolish person.
explanation.definitionFit: To nitpick is to find fault over trivial details, which is what quibbling is.

clue.text: My point is appropriated by orderly in a shameless manner

indicators.note: something appropriated is taken in by another, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: cor is a British exclamation like 'my!'
ruly is the rare opposite of unruly, so orderly
pt is the abbreviation for point

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a hospital orderly shamelessly stole their idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation, not a possessive; cor is British slang for the same surprise. 'Orderly' looks like a hospital worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting corruptly means acting dishonestly and without moral scruple, which is shameless behaviour.

clue.text: See 13
Struggle with replacing conclusion of public survey

indicators.note: replacing the conclusion means a new ending takes the place of the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: overt means open, public
to vie is to struggle or compete
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Pollsters struggle after changing the conclusion of a public opinion survey.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of the word for public is dropped and the struggle-plus-with combination takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: An overview is a general summary or review of a subject, as a survey can be.

clue.text: Cheating in sport stopped by English and European clubs first

E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Cheating in a sport is ended by English and European football clubs acting first.
explanation.walkthrough: The three single letters go between the D and the rest of the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceiving means misleading or tricking someone, much as cheating does.

clue.text: On-line gambling game incorporating Formula One's structure

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into the body, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an online version of dice, with the e- prefix for electronic
F1, motor racing's top formula, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: An online betting game features a Formula One structure.
explanation.walkthrough: E- stands for electronic, as in e-mail. Formula One's 1 becomes the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large building, so a structure in the architectural sense.

clue.text: Circular letter government's leaked about newspaper?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the abbreviation

dye that leaked from fabric ran

clue.text: Talk about limits of every component of PC's interface

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters

clue.text: Heard word my herd blurred!

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Image returned by idol out of love for nobody

clue.text: Leave work during strike

clue.text: Tyres said to be essential items for cars?

explanation.walkthrough: Tyres sounds like 'tires', meaning wears out; the car surface makes the reader think of rubber.

clue.text: Typical accident caused by race on motorway

clue.text: Time "suppressing article" in US statesman's words

clue.text: Reported vulnerable, confused state when one goes to school
